parts.text: Which claim best explains why these traditional foods differ?

options.text: Local crops, tastes, culture, and traditions shape traditional foods in each state.
States that grow the same crops must share the same traditional foods.
A state's traditional foods decide which crops, tastes, and traditions it will have.
Everyone in a state eats the same traditional food every day.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Bilal compares mustard-oil dishes common in one Indian state with coconut-oil dishes common in another.

part_answers.answer: Traditional food patterns follow locally grown crops plus tastes, culture, and traditions, so mustard-oil and coconut-oil dishes can differ across states.

teacher.key_rationale: Regional traditional foods reflect local crops, tastes, culture, and traditions. Same crops do not force identical foods, foods do not choose the crops, and not everyone in a state eats one fixed dish.
